A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diffusion Policy Policy Optimization (DPPO). Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including figures, tables, and equations, and corresponding material can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments, ablations, and hardware evaluations, including DPPO succeeding in 16 of 20 real-world trials in Section 5.4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds diffusion-policy baseline comparisons and a structured-exploration ablation in Appendices C.1 and C.7.

M1.justification: The two-layer MDP, PPO update, advantage estimator, denoising discounts, partial-step fine-tuning, and DDIM options are retained. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure; the new experimental variants do not replace the proposed DPPO method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GYM, Franka-Kitchen, Robomimic, Furniture-Bench, hardware, and D3IL Avoid coverage. The added studies reuse Can/Square with previously covered demonstration types and Avoid's existing M1–M3 settings.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates Gaussian-policy RLPD, Cal-QL, and IBRL. v3 retains those comparisons and additionally evaluates diffusion-policy adaptations of all three in Appendix C.1, Figure A1. The other comparator groups remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 adds comparisons with action chunks of 1 and 4. Appendix C.7 introduces a DDIM-based control applying noise throughout denoising versus only at the final step, with noise floors of 0.05 and 0.1 in Avoid. Existing hyperparameter tables and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Two focused diagnostic extensions are added: controlling the baseline policy parameterization in C.1 and isolating intermediate-step exploration noise in C.7. The latter supplies Avoid trajectories and Can/Square learning curves. Earlier ablations and robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and statistical reporting conventions are retained. The new Figures A1 and A11 use the established three-seed averaging practice; no new confidence-interval definition, significance test, or increased repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: New results show diffusion-policy RLPD and Cal-QL remaining unsuccessful, while IBRL learns but generally trails DPPO. Figure A11 reports faster Can/Square learning with noise throughout denoising. Figure 6 also revises plotted curves and omits previously shown later-training segments in HalfCheetah and Square; this does not establish a same-setting performance gain or loss. Hardware outcomes and runtime tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The core MDP and policy-gradient/PPO mathematics are unchanged. Appendix B spells out the previously invoked behavior-cloning, GAE, policy, and value-training formulas and standard GAE endpoints. These explain the existing implementation without adding a substantive theoretical derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: Contribution 2 refines the broad claim of consistent, marked stability improvements and frequent performance improvements into strong stability across tasks and marked final-performance improvements specifically in challenging robotic tasks. The abstract, other principal contributions, and conclusion retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explanation of successive noise injections expanding coverage while denoising pulls actions toward the demonstration manifold. Appendix C.1 further attributes baseline difficulties to Q-learning rather than policy parameterization and contrasts IBRL's data collection with direct DPPO fine-tuning. Existing applicability limits remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B expands and relocates v2's D.5 implementation discussion, adding Algorithm 1, rollout/minibatch organization, explicit GAE computation, and actor/value objectives. It also discloses that KL-based early stopping never triggered in practice. Existing hyperparameters, hardware details, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Lei et al.'s Uni-O4 and Permenter and Yuan's diffusion-optimization work. Appendix A expands offline-to-online positioning and explicitly distinguishes DPPO from Psenka et al.'s policy-gradient formulation, including an independent-development statement and different treatment of denoising steps.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to Contribution 2, mechanism explanations, related work, and implementation documentation. The implementation subsection becomes an expanded Appendix B, shifting the existing experimental, runtime, and technical appendices to C, D, and E. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds two plots, numbered A1 and A11, and the Algorithm 1 display. Figure 6 is redrawn with coarser traces and a one-million-step horizon throughout, shortening several panels previously extending to two million. Earlier appendix figures are retained under new numbers, with accompanying layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The diffusion-baseline controls and noise-location ablation provide more direct support for explanations already advanced in v2, while Algorithm 1 improves implementation clarity. These are useful, focused gains. A countervailing weakness is that Figure 6 removes later-convergence evidence while its accompanying text still emphasizes superior final performance.
